extracted.intended_audience: book-buying public, readers, librarians, collectors, and specialists interested in new historical, travel, memoir, and reference publications
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative language used in 19th-century publisher/catalogue/review notices to judge the quality, authority, and appeal of historical, travel, memoir, and reference books. Focuses on authenticity, illustrations, readability, scholarly value, and suitability for libraries or gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity / original sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Works 'from original family documents' or 'from numerous original sources' and 'including MS. Documents' are valued for providing authentic material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise is given when a book publishes original manuscripts, family archives, or unpublished sources that 'cast new jets of light' or afford 'abundant information'; authenticity enhances historical value and public gratitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value for illuminating secret or obscure history
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'clears up much secret history' and 'casts new jets of light' on events or characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical works are commended when they resolve obscure events, confirm old stories, or bring out new traits of character—i.e., when they materially advance understanding of a period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicious explanatory commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'intrinsic value of the letters is enhanced by the judicious setting of the explanatory comment that accompanies them'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/commentators should add careful, honest explanatory notes that contextualize primary documents to increase a work's usefulness and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of epoch/period coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes that 'cover a complete epoch' or 'comprehend a period the most important' are especially prized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that systematically treat a full era (e.g., the Regency, 1800–1810) are considered more valuable for libraries and historians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertaining for general readers while informative for specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: The general reader is 'entertained, and the reader for historical purposes is enlightened.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good books balance readability and entertainment with solid information suitable for scholarly use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness and painstaking scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors described as 'most painstaking and trustworthy historians' are recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful research, accuracy, and thoroughness distinguish reliable historical works and earn wide praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative appeal / readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that are 'delightful', 'impossible to leave', 'fresh', 'lively and agreeable', or 'manly in tone' are praised for style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylish, engaging prose that makes a subject absorbing is a major positive quality—often highlighted in recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and new material
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of 'new sayings, pictures, anecdotes', 'new traits', 'new and pleasant additions', or 'information hitherto unpublished.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/reviewers value material that is previously unknown or unpublished and which enriches the historical record or narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and correctness (registry/reference works)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference works are judged on 'authority, correctness', being 'an established and authentic authority', and 'corrected throughout from the personal communications of the Nobility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works of record (peerage, genealogy) must be authoritative, continually updated from primary sources, and reliable for reference purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and up-to-dateness of corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peerage's advantage: 'the type being kept constantly standing, every correction is made in its proper place to the date of publication'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works that allow prompt incorporation of corrections and updates gain supremacy over competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness / inclusion of collateral branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to collateral branches and inclusion of many names 'which do not appear in other records' is a point of excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genealogical/reference books are praised when they are more complete than rivals, covering obscure or collateral family members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and execution / editorial design
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Lodge’s Peerage must supersede all other works... for two reasons: first, it is on a better plan; and, secondly, it is better executed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sound organizational plan and high-quality execution (editing, arrangement) are key evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance of typography, binding, and production
rubrics_metrics.description: Works noted for 'beauty of its typography and binding', 'handsomely bound, with gilt edges', and 'elegant in its style' are recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical production values (typography, binding, illustrations) contribute to a book's appeal, especially for gift and library markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and usefulness of illustrations and plates
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations described as 'numerous and beautiful', 'highly coloured', 'exact representation', 'superb wood engravings', or 'hand-coloured plates' are praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality illustrations that accurately represent subjects (insignia, landscapes, scenes) greatly enhance travel, reference, and history books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly / scientific utility (for specialists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel works give 'notes and pictures' valuable to the geographer, geologist, ethnologist, botanist; maps and scientific observations add worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that supply original geographic, ethnographic, geological, or botanical information are of high scholarly value to specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness as library/reference/book-of-record
rubrics_metrics.description: Works 'must find a place in the library of every English gentleman' and are 'indispensable' as a book of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A measure of a book's success is its longevity and utility as a reference in private and public collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as gift / general tasteful qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: A travel book predicted to 'assume the shape of a Christmas Present ... as it possesses ... usefulness, elegance, instruction and novelty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination of usefulness, attractive production, instructive content, and novelty make a book appropriate as a gift item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to literature / lasting reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A contribution to literature which will have a reputation as imperishable' and works whose 'reputation is indelibly stamped.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether a work will endure and be regarded as a lasting literary or scholarly contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value from author's personal experience / eyewitness testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Books by eyewitnesses or actors in events ('told ... by eye-witnesses ... by the very men who put them in motion') earn high praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firsthand accounts, journals, soldiers' or officials' narratives are prized for immediacy and authority about events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and quality of appended primary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of 'a full appendix ... rich in letters hitherto unpublished' completes a memoir and is commended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices containing unpublished letters, documents, or notes add depth and documentary value to biographies and memoirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral, philosophical, or political relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that are 'a philosophical study for the politician and statesman' or 'let in a flood of light upon the actual origin, formation, and progress' are valuable beyond mere anecdote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that illuminate political, moral, or institutional origins are prized by readers interested in broader lessons and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of social habits and prevailing feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographies and memoirs that 'throw valuable light on the social habits and the prevalent feelings of the Elizabethan age' are considered useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical works that illuminate social life, manners, and culture of an era are important for both readers and scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral/ethical testimony from practitioner experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Prison narrative's value: testimony 'from such a quarter is full of novelty ... as a curious bit of human history ... philosophic without being dull.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experienced practitioners' humane/insightful testimony (e.g., prison governors, nurses) confers credibility and unique perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for varied readerships (amusement + instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated praise when a work is 'suitable for instruction and amusement' or 'instructed as well as amused.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing instructive content with entertaining elements broadens a book's appeal across audiences.
